title: Physics mechanics
targetPerformance: By hour 20, solve at least 16 of 20 fresh introductory mechanics problems in 50 minutes with a labeled force or motion sketch, consistent SI units, and a sign check; implement and test a no-drag projectile model.
whyItMatters: Turn a physical situation into a model with explicit forces, units, and testable predictions.

subskills.title: Units and estimation
subskills.selfCorrection: Write units before substituting and estimate powers of ten.

subskills.title: One-dimensional motion
subskills.selfCorrection: Choose a positive direction and distinguish distance from displacement.
drills: Predict velocity at the top of a throw.

subskills.title: Two-dimensional motion
subskills.why: Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
subskills.selfCorrection: Use the same elapsed time for both components.

subskills.title: Newton and free-body reasoning
subskills.why: Tie acceleration to net force, not motion alone.
subskills.selfCorrection: Draw only forces acting on the selected object.

subskills.title: Friction
subskills.why: Distinguish a static bound from sliding friction.
subskills.selfCorrection: Static friction adjusts up to its maximum; kinetic friction opposes sliding.
drills: Subtract kinetic friction from a pull.

subskills.title: Work and energy
subskills.why: Track transfers without solving every instant.
subskills.selfCorrection: Define the system and check the sign of work.

subskills.title: Momentum and collisions
subskills.why: Track a conserved vector in isolated collisions.
subskills.selfCorrection: Check external impulse and whether the collision sticks.

subskills.title: Circular motion
subskills.why: Recognize inward acceleration at constant speed.
subskills.selfCorrection: Identify the force supplying the inward net component.
drills: Check the effect of doubling speed.

resources.title: OpenStax — University Physics Volume 1
resources.why: Free mechanics chapters with force diagrams and worked examples.

resources.title: Khan Academy — Physics
resources.why: Short explanations and practice on motion, forces, and energy.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare — 8.01SC Classical Mechanics
resources.why: Worked examples and problem sets with solutions for momentum, energy, and circular motion.

resources.title: PhET — Projectile Motion
resources.why: Free simulation to test projectile predictions before and after coding the model.

barriers.fix: Attempt one prompt before consulting one short resource section.
Sketch or describe the quantities, predict sign and scale, then compute.
Record the failed assumption, use the next hint, and retry with changed numbers.
